root_cause.text: The PM sleep subsystem’s refcount-based GFP mask stacking change incorrectly treated pm_restore_gfp_mask() calls with saved_gfp_count == 0 as a warning condition, even though hibernation/uswsusp paths legitimately invoke the function defensively when no GFP restriction is active.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that 35e4a69b2003f introduced refcount-based GFP mask management “that warns when pm_restore_gfp_mask() is called with saved_gfp_count == 0,” and that “Some hibernation paths call pm_restore_gfp_mask() defensively… Before the stacking change this was a silent no-op; it now triggers a spurious WARNING”; the patch removes only the WARN_ON from `if (WARN_ON(!saved_gfp_count) || --saved_gfp_count)` to `if (!saved_gfp_count || --saved_gfp_count)`, preserving the no-op check.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the warning on zero `saved_gfp_count` in pm_restore_gfp_mask() while preserving the existing early-return behavior.
intent_record.what: The condition in pm_restore_gfp_mask() was changed from `if (WARN_ON(!saved_gfp_count) || --saved_gfp_count)` to `if (!saved_gfp_count || --saved_gfp_count)`, removing the `WARN_ON()` wrapper around the `!saved_gfp_count` check while keeping the control flow otherwise the same.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function still returns early when `saved_gfp_count` is zero or when decrementing it does not reach zero, but it no longer emits a warning when `pm_restore_gfp_mask()` is called with `saved_gfp_count` equal to zero.

grouping_result.intent: Remove the warning on zero `saved_gfp_count` in pm_restore_gfp_mask() while preserving the existing early-return behavior.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it removes the incorrect warning when pm_restore_gfp_mask() is called with saved_gfp_count == 0, while keeping the valid early return for defensive calls in hibernation/uswsusp paths.

candidates.rationale: This condition is the direct source of the vulnerability: it treats saved_gfp_count == 0 as a WARN_ON condition, even though defensive calls to pm_restore_gfp_mask() with no active GFP restriction are legitimate in hibernation/uswsusp paths.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition incorrectly flags the legitimate case of saved_gfp_count == 0 as a warning in pm_restore_gfp_mask(). The root cause states that defensive restore calls from hibernation/uswsusp may occur with no active GFP restriction, so treating zero as WARN_ON introduced the vulnerability.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet directly shows the relevant logic in both pm_restore_gfp_mask() and pm_restrict_gfp_mask(), so it is sufficient. The root cause is that defensive calls to pm_restore_gfp_mask() with no active restriction (saved_gfp_count == 0) should be allowed, but this commit explicitly treats that case as a warning. In pm_restore_gfp_mask(), the code says: `if (WARN_ON(!saved_gfp_count) || --saved_gfp_count) return;`. This means when `saved_gfp_count` is 0, `WARN_ON(!saved_gfp_count)` triggers, exactly matching the described vulnerable construct. The commit message also confirms this behavior: `Calling it when the GFP mask has not been restricted will cause it to warn.` Therefore the vulnerable logic is present. The fix is not present, because the function still warns on `saved_gfp_count == 0` instead of permitting that defensive no-op case.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet fully shows the implementations of both relevant functions, so it is sufficient to judge this commit version. The stated root cause is specifically about a later refcount-based change that treats `pm_restore_gfp_mask()` calls with `saved_gfp_count == 0` as a warning. In this commit, the code is not refcount-based at all: it uses `static gfp_t saved_gfp_mask;` and `pm_restore_gfp_mask()` only does `if (saved_gfp_mask) { gfp_allowed_mask = saved_gfp_mask; saved_gfp_mask = 0; }`. There is no warning on a defensive restore when no restriction is active; the only warning in `pm_restore_gfp_mask()` is `WARN_ON(!mutex_is_locked(&system_transition_mutex));`, which is unrelated to the root cause. Likewise, there is no `saved_gfp_count` and no `WARN_ON(saved_gfp_count == 0)`-style construct. Therefore the vulnerable construct described in the root cause is absent in this function. The fix for that specific regression is also not present here, because this code predates the refcount-based stacking change entirely rather than implementing the corrected handling for `saved_gfp_count == 0`.
